whoIsJesus.headline: Who Is Jesus?
whoIsJesus.lead: He was neither a myth nor a mere moral philosopher. Jesus of Nazareth is the singular figure of human history who changed the calendar, broke the power of death, and offers you personal reconciliation with God.

points.title: A Real Person in Human History
points.description: Jesus walked the dusty roads of first-century Judea and Galilee. Roman historians like Tacitus and Jewish chroniclers like Josephus confirm His life, ministry, and execution under Pontius Pilate outside Jerusalem.

points.title: Unrivaled Compassion
points.description: In an era of brutal stratification, Jesus touched lepers, defended the marginalized, wept with grieving sisters, and treated women, foreigners, and outcasts with radical dignity and honor.

points.title: God in Human Flesh
points.description: Jesus made audacious claims that no other religious founder dared utter: 'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30), and 'I am the way, the truth, and the life' (John 14:6). He demonstrated authority over nature, sickness, and death.

points.title: The Conquering of Death
points.description: Crucified under Roman authority, His tomb was found empty on the third morning. Over 500 eyewitnesses saw Him alive, transformed from terrified fugitives into courageous apostles who gave their lives testifying to His resurrection.

whyItMatters.headline: Why Does This Matter to You Today?
whyItMatters.lead: Every human heart hungers for three fundamental things: unconditional love, clean conscience, and lasting hope. Jesus does not offer mere advice; He gives Himself as our Savior and Redeemer.

insights.title: The Ache of Meaninglessness
insights.text: We often believe that happiness lies in the next achievement, relationship, or milestone. Yet when we reach it, the quiet void returns. C.S. Lewis observed: 'If I find in myself desires which nothing in this world can satisfy, the only logical explanation is that I was made for another world.'

insights.title: The Weight of Guilt and Regret
insights.text: Every person carries memories they wish they could undo and words they wish they could unsay. Religion tells you to work harder to balance your bad deeds with good ones. Jesus offers complete, unconditional forgiveness based on what He did for you.

insights.title: Victory Over Death and Anxiety
insights.text: The fear of death quietly casts a shadow over modern life. Because Jesus rose from the grave, physical death is no longer a dark dead-end for the believer, but a doorway into eternal glory and joy.

planOfSalvation.title: God's Boundless Love
planOfSalvation.summary: You were created on purpose, with dignity, to live in deep friendship with God.
planOfSalvation.scripture: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
planOfSalvation.explanation: God did not create humanity out of boredom or loneliness. He made you to experience His kindness, walk in His beauty, and enjoy unbroken fellowship with Him forever.

planOfSalvation.title: The Broken Connection
planOfSalvation.summary: Our self-centeredness and sin have separated us from a holy, perfect God.
planOfSalvation.scripture: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
planOfSalvation.explanation: Sin isn't merely breaking a list of rules; it is declaring independence from our Creator. Just as unplugging a lamp from the outlet cuts off light, cutting ourselves off from God brings spiritual darkness, moral frailty, and eternal separation.

planOfSalvation.title: The Unbreakable Bridge
planOfSalvation.summary: Jesus took our penalty upon Himself on the Cross and rose victorious over the grave.
planOfSalvation.scripture: God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
planOfSalvation.explanation: God’s justice and God’s mercy met at the Cross. Jesus lived the sinless life we failed to live and paid the debt of death we deserved, removing every barrier between you and God.

planOfSalvation.title: Grace as a Free Gift
planOfSalvation.summary: Salvation cannot be bought, earned, or deserved. It is received purely by faith.
planOfSalvation.scripture: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
planOfSalvation.explanation: You don't clean yourself up before you take a shower; you get in the shower to be cleansed. You don't have to fix your life before coming to Jesus; you come to Him broken, and He makes you new.

planOfSalvation.title: The Personal Invitation
planOfSalvation.summary: God stands at the door of your heart and invites you to receive Him today.
planOfSalvation.scripture: If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
planOfSalvation.explanation: Faith is more than intellectual agreement. It is an sincere act of trust, placing your life into the hands of the Savior who gave His life for you.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: Can I trust the historical reliability of the Bible?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: Yes. The New Testament has exponentially more manuscript evidence than any other ancient Greco-Roman text (over 5,800 Greek manuscripts, compared to fewer than 250 for Homer's Iliad or Plato's dialogues). Archaeology repeatedly confirms biblical locations, rulers, and cultural practices, and the texts were written by eyewitnesses within living memory of the events.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: If God is good and all-powerful, why is there so much suffering?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: Suffering is the hardest question in human experience. Much suffering stems from humanity's free choices to harm one another. But crucially, the Christian God did not remain distant from our pain. In Jesus, God entered our suffering, bled, wept, and suffered unjustly. He promises that one day He will wipe away every tear and make all things new.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: Have I committed too many bad things to be forgiven?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: No. The Apostle Paul persecuted and killed Christians before encountering Christ, yet became God's chosen messenger of grace. Jesus said, 'Whoever comes to me I will never cast out' (John 6:37). God's ocean of grace is far deeper than the puddle of your past mistakes.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: Don't all religions basically teach the same thing?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: While many world religions share common ethical values (like love and honesty), their core claims about reality and salvation are fundamentally contradictory. Eastern philosophies view history as cyclical and individual identity as an illusion; Islam teaches that salvation depends on whether your good deeds outweigh bad deeds on a scale. Jesus alone proclaimed that salvation is not a ladder you climb to reach God, but God descending to reach you.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: Is faith at war with scientific inquiry?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: Not at all. Modern science was birthed predominantly by Christian thinkers (like Isaac Newton, Johannes Kepler, Blaise Pascal, and Francis Bacon) who believed an orderly, rational God created an intelligible universe governed by natural laws. Science explains 'how' mechanisms operate; God explains 'why' existence, consciousness, and moral truth exist.

doubtsAndFaqs.question: What if I accept Jesus but still experience doubts later?
doubtsAndFaqs.answer: Doubt is not the opposite of faith; cynicism is. In Mark 9:24, a father cried out to Jesus, 'I believe; help my unbelief!' and Jesus answered his request. God does not demand emotional perfection or instant complete knowledge; He welcomes honest questions and walks with you through uncertainty.
